name.en: Parcel delivery text: “update your address to get your parcel”

how.en: A text or email that looks like it is from Australia Post or another courier says your parcel couldn’t be delivered or your address needs updating. It has a link to a fake website that asks for personal details or a small payment. Scammers use the details for identity theft and fraud. Australia Post never calls, texts or emails to ask for payment or personal or financial details.

text.en: A text or email says it is from Australia Post or a courier.
It says your parcel couldn’t be delivered or your address must be updated quickly.
It has a link to a site that looks official.
The site asks for your details or a small fee to redeliver.
AusPost: Your parcel could not be delivered due to an incomplete address. Please update your details within 24 hrs: [link]

en: A delivery message with a link.
Being asked to pay a small fee or update details.
Don’t click the link. Check your delivery in the official Australia Post app or website, or the courier’s own site.
If you entered card details, contact your bank straight away.
If you gave ID details such as a licence or passport, contact IDCARE.

sources.title: Expecting a delivery during the holiday sales? Stop and think, don’t click the link
